input.summary: Narrow the non-solicit to a mutual, 12-month restriction on involved personnel with advertising carve-out and no no-hire
input.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept one-way no-hire provisions; we have made the restriction mutual, limited it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months, and added the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-applicant carve-out (which Section 12.3 already preserves).

ops.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other Party who was directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This Section does not restrict either Party from hiring a person who responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment effort not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or who approaches the hiring Party on an unsolicited basis.

input.summary: Add a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us no right to exit a three-year term without cause (the numbering even skips 9.4), so we have added a Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; Vendor takes no reciprocal mid-term exit.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or further volume or payment obligation, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

input.summary: Replace Singapore law/venue with New York law, aligning with Section 28.2
input.comment: [Playbook] Our accepted governing laws are New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales, and Section 28.1 also directly conflicts with the exclusive New York County venue in Section 28.2; we have changed the governing law to New York and left 28.2 to govern venue.

ops.oldText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

input.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; delete the revocable term licence
input.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so Vendor assigns each Deliverable to us; Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 with the perpetual licence in Section 13.2. Our fallback is Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.

ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each such Deliverable upon creation. To the extent any such assignment is ineffective, Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, transferable licence to use, modify, and sublicense the Deliverable for Customer's business.
